assigned.title: WebView2 paints an opaque background over the video: criterion 2 fails while mpv is blameless
assigned.acceptance:
THE RESULT THIS IS FILED AGAINST IS DECISIVE AND IT IS A FAILURE. The commander's Round-123 run on real hardware proves: the child HWND geometry is correct at 1280x720; the local HEVC file opens; D3D11 initialises on an RTX 3050; d3d11va hardware decoding is active; the VO is gpu-next at 1280x720; the first video frame is reported shown; and the Pause button reaches mpv. Criterion 1 (hardware decode) PASS. Criterion 3 (click and control) PASS. And yet the commander sees NO VIDEO AT ALL -- only the WebView UI. Criterion 2 (compositing) FAILS and Experiment 1a is NOT PASS.

WHAT THAT COMBINATION RULES OUT. mpv is exonerated end to end: it decoded on the GPU, it configured a video output on the child HWND at the right size, and it says it put a frame on screen. The child window is the right size in the right place. The IPC path works. The only thing left between a frame mpv has drawn and a commander who cannot see it is what is painted on top of it, and that is the WebView2 surface.

WHY TAURI'S transparent: true IS NOT ENOUGH, which is the fact this round turns on. transparent: true makes the TOP-LEVEL window layered. It does not stop the WebView2 control inside that window from painting its own default background -- an opaque white -- across its whole surface. A sibling child HWND at HWND_BOTTOM is behind the WebView2 surface in z-order, so an opaque WebView2 background hides it completely. That is exactly the symptom: UI visible, video invisible, no error anywhere.

REQUIRED: THE FALLBACK DOCUMENTED IN experiments/exp-1a/README.md SECTION 10 STEP 2, TAKEN. Reach the underlying WebView2 controller through Tauri's with_webview, query it for ICoreWebView2Controller2, and call put_DefaultBackgroundColor with a fully transparent colour -- COREWEBVIEW2_COLOR { A: 0, R: 0, G: 0, B: 0 }. This is the documented Microsoft API for the exact problem and it is the move the harness's own README already named as the next one.

REQUIRED: THE THREE OUTCOMES ARE DISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE DIAGNOSTIC LOG ALONE. Success, a failed call, and a WebView2 runtime too old to offer ICoreWebView2Controller2 at all must each produce a different line through the Diag that PL-0748 already built. ICoreWebView2Controller2 is a later revision of the interface Tauri hands out, so it has to be queried for, and a runtime that does not offer it is a real possibility that must report itself in words rather than as a silent no-op. No new diagnostic infrastructure -- this is three calls to machinery that exists.

REQUIRED: NOTHING ELSE CHANGES. Same child HWND. Same HWND_BOTTOM z-order. Same WS_CLIPSIBLINGS. Same mpv property set. Same geometry, including PL-0749's corrected create_child and the single fit_child after mpv init. Same diagnostic logging. Same window configuration. The commander's instruction is explicit on this point and it is also correct: the experiment asks about one arrangement, and a round that altered the arrangement while fixing the background would answer a different question.

REQUIRED: NO NEW DEPENDENCY VERSIONS. webview2-com and windows-core are already in experiments/exp-1a/Cargo.lock as transitive dependencies of tauri at 0.39.1 and 0.62.2. They become direct dependencies at exactly those pinned versions, so the lockfile moves by the dependency edges and nothing else -- the same bar PL-0748 met when libmpv2-sys was promoted and the lock diff was a single added line with zero version drift.

REQUIRED: README.md STOPS DESCRIBING THE FALLBACK AS UN-BUILT. It currently tells the commander the fallback is not pre-built and names it as the next move. It is now built, and the README must say what the harness does, what the new log lines mean, and that this is the last corrective round.

MUST NOT: mark Experiment 1a PASS, mark PW-0103 PASS, or change decision D1. Compiling proves nothing about compositing. Even a run that finally shows video is criteria 1, 2 and 3 observed on one machine by one person, and the seven criteria and the OS/GPU/DPI matrix remain unmet.

MUST NOT: ADD A WORKAROUND LAYER BEYOND THIS ONE. The commander's instruction is terminal and this task inherits it: if video still does not appear beneath the WebView after explicit WebView2 transparency, Experiment 1a is recorded FAIL and decision D1 (native playback architecture) returns to gpt-architect. No further layers -- no DWM compositing tricks, no layered-window games, no moving mpv into its own top-level window, no swapping the z-order. At that point the honest answer is that the Tauri arrangement does not support the compositing the product needs, and that answer is worth more than another round of workarounds.
assigned.notes: FILED 2026-10-06 from the commander's Round-123 run, which is the third real-hardware run of this harness and the first whose failure is NOT in the harness's own plumbing. PL-0748 (instrumentation) and PL-0749 (geometry) are both BLOCKED rather than DONE because each holds this file and neither can reach DONE without gpt-architect's verdict; their block reasons record that in full, including that both are complete and both were proven correct by the very runs that found the next defect. That is two parked tasks on one file and it is a real debt on the board. THIS IS THE LAST CORRECTIVE ROUND. The commander has set the terminal condition: if this does not make video appear, Experiment 1a is FAIL and D1 goes back to architecture review.

build.evidence:
cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -D warnings: clean for BOTH x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and the host. repo:validate passed.

THE NEW CODE IS REALLY COMPILED FOR WINDOWS, proved rather than assumed: replacing the A field of the COREWEBVIEW2_COLOR literal with a string produced E0308 for the Windows target, and was then reverted. Every line of this change lives behind #[cfg(windows)] and would otherwise be invisible to a check run in this container.

THE LOCKFILE MOVED BY EXACTLY TWO LINES, and they are both dependency edges. webview2-com and windows-core went from transitive dependencies of tauri to direct dependencies of exp-1a, so "webview2-com" and "windows-core" were added to exp-1a's dependency list and nothing else. A package-by-package comparison of the before and after locks reports moved: none, added: none, removed: none, 384 packages before and 384 after. No version drifted and --locked is honoured. Same bar PL-0748 met when libmpv2-sys was promoted.

WHAT CHANGED, and it is one thing. clear_webview_background() reaches the underlying WebView2 controller through Tauri's with_webview, queries it for ICoreWebView2Controller2 via windows_core::Interface::cast, and calls SetDefaultBackgroundColor with COREWEBVIEW2_COLOR { A: 0, R: 0, G: 0, B: 0 }. It is called once in run()'s setup closure, before create_child, so the first paint after the video child appears is already a transparent one.

THE THREE OUTCOMES ARE SEPARATELY REPORTED, through PL-0748's existing Diag and with no new infrastructure: the colour was set; the call was made and refused; or ICoreWebView2Controller2 is not available because the installed WebView2 runtime predates the API. The third is a real possibility on a real machine and the log says in words that it is a runtime-version result and NOT a compositing result, so it cannot be mistaken for an Experiment 1a failure. A fourth line covers with_webview failing to reach the webview at all.

THE API SURFACE WAS READ, NOT GUESSED. tauri-2.12.0 src/webview/mod.rs:184 declares PlatformWebview::controller() -> ICoreWebView2Controller under #[cfg(windows)]; webview_window.rs:2503 declares WebviewWindow::with_webview under feature "wry", and "wry" is in tauri 2.12.0's default feature set, which this Cargo.toml does not disable. webview2-com-sys-0.39.1 src/bindings.rs:196 declares COREWEBVIEW2_COLOR { A, R, G, B } and line 9889 declares SetDefaultBackgroundColor on impl ICoreWebView2Controller2. windows-core-0.62.2 src/interface.rs:92 declares Interface::cast. webview2-com does not re-export windows-core, which is why windows-core is a direct dependency rather than reached through it.

WHAT DID NOT CHANGE, deliberately and because the commander's instruction is explicit on it: the child HWND, HWND_BOTTOM, WS_CLIPSIBLINGS, the geometry including PL-0749's corrected create_child and the single fit_child after mpv init, the mpv property set, the diagnostic logging and the window configuration. The experiment asks about one arrangement and a round that altered the arrangement while fixing the background would answer a different question.

README.md stops describing the fallback as un-built, states what the harness now does, explains what each of the three new log lines means, and records that this is the last corrective round.

NOT CLAIMED, and this is the whole point: that any of it makes video appear. Nothing here has run. Experiment 1a is NOT PASS, PW-0103 is untouched and D1 is unchanged. Even a run that finally shows video is criteria 1, 2 and 3 observed on one machine by one person; the seven criteria and the OS/GPU/DPI matrix are unmet.
